title: Conductor power for the normalization of a one-dimensional semilocal domain
statement: Let B be a commutative Noetherian semilocal domain of Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and K its fraction field. Write B' for the integral closure of B in K [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] and assume B' has finitely many maximal ideals. For x,y in B', if x is nonzero and lies in the Jacobson radical of B', there exist n > 0 and b in B with algebraMap B K b = x^n y in K.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2, finite-conductor and Jacobson-radical paragraphs

proof.text: Apply the finite-adjoin/Jacobson-power auxiliary theorem to obtain a finite intermediate subalgebra A containing x and y, a positive m, and a in the mapped Jacobson ideal with a = x^m.
Apply the ideal-power conductor multiplication theorem to a^r and y, where r is the positive conductor exponent for A, and rewrite (x^m)^r as x^(m*r).

proof_origin.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2; finite-adjoin and conductor-power reduction

from.place: 09N2 conductor-power conclusion, separated from the normalization clause

lean.statement:
theorem semilocal_dim_one_conductor_power
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum B)] (hdim : ringKrullDim B = 1)
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra B K] [IsFractionRing B K]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum (integralClosure B K))] :
    ∀ x y : integralClosure B K,
      x ≠ 0 → x ∈ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal (integralClosure B K)) →
        ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∃ b : B,
          algebraMap B K b = (x : K) ^ n * (y : K)
